paper_title: The Equivalence, Unambiguity and Sequentiality Problems of Finitely Ambiguous Max-Plus Tree Automata are Decidable
statement: 4 The Unambiguity Problem The unambiguity problem asks whether for a given max-plus-WTA A there exists an unambiguous max-plus-WTA A0 such that JAK = JA0 K. In this section, we show that the unambiguity problem is decidable for finitely ambiguous max-plus-WTA. We follow ideas from [11, Section 5], where the decidability of this problem was shown for finitely ambiguous max-plus word automata. The unambiguity problem is, in fact, even known to be decidable for polynomially ambiguous max-plus word automata [10]. We leave the question open as to whether the same holds true for polynomially ambiguous max-plus-WTA.

For a finitely ambiguous max-plus-WTA A it is decidable whether there exists an unambiguous max-plus-WTA A0 with JAK = JA0 K. If A0 exists, it can be effectively constructed.
